listings.title: HUD Tenant Rights & Lease Basics
listings.summary: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development overview of tenant rights, leases, security deposits, and fair housing.
listings.source: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
steps: Learn your federal fair-housing rights before signing anything.
Read the full lease carefully; never sign a blank form.
Confirm who is responsible for repairs and maintenance.
Check security-deposit limits and return rules for your state.
Get every agreement and landlord promise in writing.
Keep copies of the lease, move-in checklist, and all notices.

listings.title: Indiana Tenant Rights Handbook
listings.summary: Indiana-specific guide to tenant rights, leases, eviction process, and security deposits from Indiana Legal Services.
steps: Review the Indiana Tenant Rights Handbook for your county.
Check your lease for illegal clauses before signing.
Document the unit's condition with photos at move-in.
Know the Indiana eviction notice timeline and your response window.
Keep a paper trail of rent payments and landlord communications.

listings.title: USA.gov Tenant Rights
listings.summary: Federal USA.gov guide to tenant rights, leases, security deposits, and where to find local help.
steps: Visit USA.gov/tenant-rights for the federal renter overview.
Review your lease terms and state security-deposit rules.
Find your state or local tenant-rights office through the directory.
Document repair requests and keep dated copies.
Contact a local legal-aid office if your landlord violates the lease.

listings.title: Repair Request Letter Template
listings.summary: Template for notifying your landlord in writing about needed repairs, with steps to document and follow up.
steps: Document the issue with photos and dates.
Write a dated repair-request letter describing the problem clearly.
Reference your lease clause requiring landlord maintenance.
Keep a copy and send it by certified mail or hand-deliver with a receipt.
Allow a reasonable time for repairs, then follow up in writing.

listings.title: Indiana Repair-and-Deduct Notice Guide
listings.summary: Indiana Legal Services guidance on repair-and-deduct options when a landlord fails to make essential repairs.
steps: Confirm the repair affects health, safety, or habitability.
Notify the landlord in writing and keep proof of delivery.
Review Indiana Legal Services repair-and-deduct rules for your situation.
Document all repair costs with receipts before deducting.
Contact Indiana Legal Services before withholding or deducting rent.

listings.title: Find Free Local Legal Aid
listings.summary: LawHelp.org directory to locate free civil legal aid and tenant-rights assistance by state.
steps: Go to LawHelp.org and select your state.
Search for housing or tenant-rights legal aid programs.
Check income eligibility for free services.
Gather your lease, notices, and repair documentation.
Contact the legal aid office to request assistance.

listings.title: HUD Move-In Condition Checklist
listings.summary: HUD move-in checklist to record a rental unit's condition and protect your security deposit.
listings.source: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
steps: Complete the checklist with your landlord before moving in.
Walk through every room and note existing damage.
Photograph walls, floors, appliances, and fixtures.
Have both you and the landlord sign and date the checklist.
Keep a signed copy for your records.

listings.title: Indiana Move-Out Checklist & Security Deposit
listings.summary: Indiana Legal Services checklist for moving out, cleaning, final walkthrough, and security-deposit return.
steps: Review your lease move-out and notice requirements.
Clean the unit and remove all personal belongings.
Complete a final walkthrough with the landlord if possible.
Take dated photos of the empty, cleaned unit.
Provide your forwarding address in writing for the deposit return.

listings.title: Security Deposit Return Checklist
listings.summary: USA.gov guidance on getting your security deposit back after moving out.
steps: Know your state's deadline for security-deposit returns.
Submit your forwarding address to the landlord in writing.
Document the unit condition with move-out photos.
Request an itemized list if any deposit is withheld.
Dispute improper charges through local legal aid if needed.

listings.title: Responding to an Indiana Eviction Notice
listings.summary: Indiana Legal Services guidance on how to respond when you receive an eviction notice.
steps: Read the eviction notice carefully and note the deadline.
Do not ignore the notice; respond within the time window.
Contact Indiana Legal Services or a local legal-aid office immediately.
Gather your lease, payment records, and landlord communications.
Appear for any scheduled court date if one is set.
